summary: Implemented packet 54 on the existing wasm shell and host contract. Rust views own sign-in steps, navigation, drafts, pending saves and rejected-name recovery; browser_session::Sessions, account sign_in/resolve/revoke, host access policy and store::rename_item_at_revision remain authoritative. Shared native/wasm wire types are reused without bringing the blocking client into wasm. Stock Kit Input/Button controls supply the interactions; no custom visual control, parallel API or second session mechanism was added. The approved Rust accessibility adapter consumes GPUI's real tree, forwards actions, removes stale nodes and protects password input through the platform IME receiver. Public checksum-verified preparation reproduces the necessary gpui-pre/gpui-pre-web 0.3.14 patches outside Cargo's shared cache; scripts/dev.ps1 now performs that preparation for clean Windows checkouts. Unrelated existing work was preserved. Documentation changes are limited to the affected auth/list workflow row and this handoff; protected process documents, runner gates and verification markers were not edited. No commit, push or deployment was performed.
evidence: Final focused command: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features web-smoke --test web_auth_board --test web_auth_preflight --test web_shell -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed all 8 browser cases: 4 auth-board cases in 78.40 seconds, 1 accessibility preflight in 11.95 seconds and 3 inherited shell regressions in 35.79 seconds. Every target reported 0 failed, ignored or filtered cases. Each browser journey used an owned Chromium profile, host and synthetic rustday_test schema with independent PostgreSQL connections for accepted state.

web_auth_accessibility_preflight passed as an enabled standalone regression and its action checkpoint ran inside every auth-board journey. Chromium exposed the stock Check session button by role/name; activating its AX-derived node reached GPUI and produced exactly one session GET followed by one board-list GET. The standalone accepted screen exposed 13 nodes and 3 buttons; the catalog screen exposed 15 nodes and 6 buttons. The adapter derives nodes from GPUI updates, not an application-maintained control list.

web_signs_in_lists_and_logs_out passed: identifier advancement made no account request; unknown-identifier and wrong-password submissions produced the same correctable rejection with zero stored sessions. Correction resolved before listing. Visible UUID/name rows matched the independent stored Quartz/Review/Review order and grant checks. Removed membership yielded No boards; a real catalog lock yielded an unavailable list with retry. A failed logout retained the list and current verifier. Acknowledged logout removed only that verifier, while a separately issued peer token still resolved.

web_opens_board_and_rejects_stale_access passed: UUID selection, reload after membership removal, explicit destination retry, Back/Forward and direct /web/boards/{uuid} entry requested current session/access instead of reusing stale rows. Denial exposed no item UUID controls. Signed-out direct entry retained the destination through sign-in and resolved before reading that board. Stored grants and both boards were checked independently.

web_renames_and_recovers_rejection passed: F2/Escape cancellation and unchanged Enter sent no PUT. Blank blur and explicit read-before-retry both rejected without changing Ink/1. Enter committed the trimmed Coral/2 once; blur committed Review/3 once. A real database constraint refused Quartz and retained Review/3; after removing the constraint, explicit retry issued GET before PUT and committed Quartz/4. Independent reconnects checked both ordered item identities and revisions, the sibling board and grants. Dismiss sent no request. Logout after editing removed the former editor context from Chromium's accessibility text.

web_restores_session_in_a_second_tab passed: an independent same-origin tab resolved before its addressed board GET, displayed the independently stored rows and retained the same sole verifier. Acknowledged logout cleared protected controls in both first-origin tabs and left no account session. Each tab was brought to the foreground before inspecting its live rendered accessibility tree; background-tab painting is not claimed.

Password regression passed while editing and after submission: generated secrets were absent both from individual AX values and from concatenated accessibility text descendants. The platform keeps only one attached IME receiver, switches to a native protected input for GPUI password focus without copying values between receiver types, and retains the existing GPUI input/action owner. Session-change broadcasts contain no credentials. The driver receives generated credentials through stdin, never argv, URLs or logs.

All 3 inherited web_shell cases passed on the final implementation: existing-session reload, unavailable/rejected resolution with keyboard retry, and document/module/wasm cross-origin isolation. Existing canvas/frame, HttpOnly cookie metadata, same-origin traffic, runtime-error and dependency-boundary assertions remained enabled. The transitional preview was retained unchanged. Successful fixture teardown checked the owned browser exit and profile removal; host/schema cleanup remained fixture-owned.

crates/web/test-prepare-platform.ps1 passed, including the final repeat: a fresh isolated fixture containing only public preparation inputs reproduced every accepted file in both patched platform sources from checksum-verified public crates, then repeated preparation idempotently. It did not read private project settings or alter Cargo's shared source cache. On a clean Windows checkout, dot-source scripts/dev.ps1 before ordinary locked Cargo commands; it prepares the ignored .deps sources referenced by the workspace patches.

cargo +nightly-2026-10-31 check --locked -p boardcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown passed with the protected receiver. The final browser suites also built the actual Trunk wasm bundle with --locked. Their final development bundle measured 134235795 bytes; this is not a release/compressed performance measurement.

cargo check --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --bin boardcraft-desktop passed, compiling the native consumer of the same core accessibility patch. cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-client --lib passed both existing access-hint/revision-header tests, with 0 ignored or filtered cases. No native graphical interaction evidence is inferred from compilation.

Final native lint: cargo clippy --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-client -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host -p boardcraft-web --all-targets --features web-smoke -- -D warnings passed. Final wasm/platform lint: cargo +nightly-2026-10-31 clippy --locked -p boardcraft-web -p gpui-pre-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib -- -D warnings passed.

Final cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo fmt --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml -- --check, rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for both authored platform modules, node --check crates/mobile-edit-host/tests/web/drive.mjs and git diff --check all passed. Diff statistics and new source sizes were inspected; generated dependency sources and bundle output remain ignored.

Intermediate checks were not passing evidence: initial wasm checks exposed unsupported send_blocking calls, patch-anchor/API mistakes and a missing trait import; these were corrected. One initial standalone preflight attempt exceeded its 120-second command timeout; subsequent runs completed normally with a larger outer timeout. An initial auth suite passed 3/4 because the independent tab was inspected while backgrounded. Stronger later regressions found real split-node password exposure, unchanged Enter reopening the editor and a clipped logout action; those failed focused runs were retained as regressions and fixed with a protected receiver, Enter capture and persistent global actions. The receiver preparation also initially had a missing delimiter, caught by the wasm check and fixed. Wasm lint initially rejected a nested conditional, which was corrected. Final checks above passed without ignoring, removing or weakening these cases.

Read-only node scripts/run.mjs status reported packet 53 verified and packet 54 pending. No runner or verification-marker changes were made by this worker. Full locked workspace verification and inherited Windows/Android graphical suites were intentionally not run: the runner owns full verification once at handoff. A real screen-reader run, wider role/action coverage, touch/IME composition, theme/zoom fidelity, browser/host restart, release performance and deployment remain unverified. No attended input or shared clipboard was used. Existing packet 26/27/29/30 expectations and synthetic fixtures were reused; no new executed reference comparison is claimed.
